post-fĕro , ferre, v. a.,
I.to put after, to esteem less (not before the Aug. period): “qui libertati plebis suas opes postferrent,” sacrificed, Liv. 3, 64, 3 : “Vatinius nulli non postferendus (opp.: Brutus cuilibet praeferendus),” Vell. 2, 69, 3 : “postferte fidem regnis,” Sil. 2, 701 : “non postferuntur et Charites,” Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 32 ; 4, 4, 5, § 9: “animi et corporis robore nulli juvenum postferendus,” Curt. 7, 4, 17 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
